extra.message: SQL text is built by interpolating a value. If that value comes from a request, an attacker can change the query (SQL injection). Use a placeholder (`?`) and pass the value as a bound parameter.

HTML is assembled from a variable and written straight to the response. If the value comes from the request this is reflected cross-site scripting (XSS). HTML-escape the value or use a template engine that escapes by default.

A shell command string is built from a variable and run with child_process.exec, which invokes /bin/sh. A value like `x; rm -rf ~` runs extra commands (OS command injection). Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and validate the input.
MD5/SHA-1 are broken for security use and are fast to brute-force. Switch to SHA-256 at minimum; for passwords prefer scrypt/argon2 with a per-user salt.

metadata.title: Weak hash algorithm (MD5/SHA-1)
metadata.fix_summary: Swap MD5/SHA-1 for SHA-256. A stopgap: password storage should move to scrypt or argon2 with a salt (needs a data migration).

extra.message: Math.random() is predictable and must not be used for session tokens, reset links or other secrets. Use crypto.randomBytes (or crypto.randomUUID).

metadata.title: Predictable random value used as a token
metadata.fix_summary: Generate the token with crypto.randomBytes (a CSPRNG) instead of Math.random.

extra.message: `eval` is used to parse data. Any JavaScript in the input runs with the server's privileges (code injection). The input is a JSON-style literal, so JSON.parse is a drop-in replacement.

metadata.title: eval() used to parse data
metadata.fix_summary: Parse the value with JSON.parse instead of eval, so the input can no longer run code.
